message: "orders"."seq" is added as a serial column, which rewrites the whole "orders" table while blocking reads and writes.
why: The new value must be computed for every existing row, so PostgreSQL rewrites the table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. A constant default, or a stable one such as now(), does not need a rewrite.
safeAlternative: Add the column as a plain integer, create a sequence, and set the default with ALTER COLUMN ... SET DEFAULT nextval(...), which applies only to new rows. Then backfill existing rows in batches.

message: "orders"."total" is added as a stored generated column, which rewrites the whole "orders" table while blocking reads and writes.
why: The new value must be computed for every existing row, so PostgreSQL rewrites the table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. A constant default, or a stable one such as now(), does not need a rewrite.
safeAlternative: Add a plain nullable column, fill it in batches (for identity: attach a sequence as the default first), and switch the application to it. Avoid adding computed columns to large tables in place.
